destinations.title: How is a KK-graviton population produced?
destinations.question: Can a hot Standard Model brane gravitationally produce the KK-graviton abundance needed in the Dark Dimension setting?
destinations.summary: The source studies initially unexcited bulk modes coupled to a hot Standard Model brane. Initial production and abundance are a distinct question from whether the produced population can subsequently cascade rapidly enough to remain viable dark matter.

excludes: late-time linear perturbation constraints as the primary target
regimes: Dark Dimension setup; source-specific cosmological assumptions

destinations.title: What controls the near-threshold cascade rate?
destinations.question: How does an intra-tower KK-graviton decay amplitude and rate scale with daughter momentum near threshold, and which background or coupling assumptions control that scaling?
destinations.summary: Two late-2026 sources in the frozen corpus argue for stronger threshold suppression than assumed in earlier rapid-cascade estimates. One studies cancellations and their scope in scalar–gravity systems; the other emphasizes the partial-wave interpretation and applies it to a flat dark dimension. Their contribution to this common question does not require treating their entire claims or regimes as equivalent.

excludes: unqualified universal statement for every field content or higher-derivative theory
automatic equivalence of all cosmological conclusions
assumptions: source-specific diffeomorphism-invariant couplings and background assumptions
regimes: near-threshold two-body decay; detailed paper-specific scope retained
conventions: Different momentum symbols must be identified in the parent rest frame before comparing threshold scalings.

destinations.title: What would repeated decays do to cosmological structure?
destinations.question: Within the specified repeated-decay KK-graviton model, how do daughter recoil and the changing mass distribution affect linear cosmological perturbations?
destinations.summary: The 2023 analysis propagates a simplified decay-driven population through linear cosmology and constrains a kick-velocity combination. Its observational calculation should be read together with the assumed cascade dynamics. The later threshold-rate question tests a premise of the rapid-cascade scenario; it is a separate connected destination.

excludes: new observational data beyond the frozen source
unconditional viability of the underlying cascade model
regimes: linear cosmological regime; dated source model and observations

destinations.title: What bounds survive if the cascade is suppressed?
destinations.question: In a flat dark dimension with threshold-suppressed KK-graviton cascades, what observational constraints follow from the irreducibly produced population even if it is not all dark matter?
destinations.summary: The 2026 source studies photon emission from an unavoidable freeze-in population and compares the resulting upper reheating bound with lower cosmological bounds. This asks a different question from fitting linear structure in the earlier fast-cascade model. The stated flat-dimension scope must remain visible.

excludes: all extra-dimensional models excluded without a scope argument
unqualified replacement of every earlier cosmological calculation
assumptions: near-threshold cascade suppression as argued in source
regimes: source-specific freeze-in/decay cosmology and observational assumptions
